subject: english

concepts.title: Parental Role Modeling and Self-Worth
concepts.definition: The deliberate effort of a parent to act with absolute honesty and moral rectitude to serve as an exemplary model for their child's upbringing.
concepts.key_idea: Children imitate their parents, making parental integrity crucial for a child's moral development.
question_patterns: How does Tao Ying's behavior change when she is with her son compared to when she is alone?
Why does Tao Ying feel a sense of responsibility when touching her son's head?
Explain the concept of parental role modeling as depicted in One Centimetre.
What does Tao Ying mean by carrying an audience with her wherever she goes?
Analyze how Tao Ying's desire to be an ideal mother affects her daily choices.

solution_steps.explain: Tao Ying is astute and frugal when alone, but strictly rule-abiding and exemplary when accompanied by her son.
She views herself as the center of her son's universe and wants to set a perfect, flawless example for him.
Acting graciously and setting a moral example elevates her sense of self-worth and dignity.

concepts.title: Childhood Self-Esteem and Economic Value
concepts.definition: The prioritization of a child's dignity, self-worth, and emotional happiness over minor financial savings or material benefits.
concepts.key_idea: Purchasing a ticket can represent buying self-esteem and validation for a child rather than just paying a fare.
question_patterns: Why does Tao Ying insist on buying a ticket for Xiao Ye even when he is under the height limit?
What does the author mean by purchasing self-esteem with twenty cents?
How does the ticket purchase on the bus reflect the conflict between economy and pride?
Analyze the purchasing power of twenty cents in Tao Ying's household budget.
Why was the ticket so important to Xiao Ye's sense of dignity?

solution_steps.action: State the cost of the ticket and its opportunity cost
solution_steps.explain: The ticket costs twenty cents, which could otherwise buy essential food items like cucumbers, tomatoes, or spinach.

solution_steps.action: Describe the child's desire for validation
solution_steps.explain: Xiao Ye wants his growth and status recognized, viewing the ticket as a symbol of being grown up.
Tao Ying chooses to spend the money to preserve her son's happiness and self-esteem, which is far more valuable than the monetary saving.

concepts.title: Arbitrary Institutional Standards and Height Limits
concepts.definition: The enforcement of rigid, physical benchmarks by public bodies to regulate access and fees, often leading to disputes over minor discrepancies.
concepts.key_idea: Physical height thresholds serve as arbitrary boundaries for childhood benefits.
question_patterns: How is the 1.10 meter height limit used as a regulatory tool in the story?
Describe the significance of the painted finger and the red line on the wall.
Why does the guard at the temple insist that Xiao Ye needs a ticket?
Discuss the arbitrary nature of height-based ticketing rules in public transport and temples.
How does the temple guard justify his measurement of Xiao Ye?

solution_steps.explain: The rule states that children under 1.10 meters (110 cm) are exempt from purchasing tickets.

solution_steps.action: Describe how the rule is visually enforced
solution_steps.explain: It is marked by a painted finger on the bus door and a red line resembling an earthworm on the temple wall.

solution_steps.action: Analyze the conflict arising from rigid enforcement
solution_steps.explain: Minor variations in posture, hair, or inaccurate measurement markers lead to disputes and accusations of dishonesty.

concepts.title: Deceptive Metrics and Flattering Scales
concepts.definition: The commercial practice of using intentionally miscalibrated measuring devices to flatter customers by showing desirable but false readings.
concepts.key_idea: Inaccurate scales are used commercially to flatter customers' desires to be taller or lighter.
question_patterns: Why did the old woman's scales show Xiao Ye's height as one metre eleven?
What are flattering scales or fitness scales according to the old woman?
Explain the convoluted logic behind the old lady's measurements.
How did the old woman's inaccurate scale create a conflict between Tao Ying and her son?
Why did Xiao Ye trust the old woman's scale over his mother's word?

solution_steps.action: Explain the calibration of the old woman's scales
solution_steps.explain: The scales were intentionally adjusted to make people look lighter and taller to make them happy.
The scale measured Xiao Ye at 1.11 meters, which was taller than his actual height of 1.09 meters.
This commercial deception made Xiao Ye believe his mother was lying to save money, destroying his trust in her.

concepts.title: Maternal Vindication and Institutional Redress
concepts.definition: The pursuit of moral clearance and truth by an individual to restore their child's trust and vindicate themselves from false accusations of dishonesty.
concepts.key_idea: Restoring a child's trust is more valuable than monetary compensation or free tickets.
question_patterns: Why did Tao Ying write a letter to the temple administrators?
What did the temple officials find when they measured Xiao Ye at his home?
Why did Tao Ying refuse the five-dollar compensation and free tickets offered by the officials?
What was the ultimate vindication that Tao Ying sought from the temple officials?
How does the ending of the story highlight the importance of maternal dignity?

solution_steps.action: Identify the purpose of Tao Ying's letter
solution_steps.explain: She wrote to the administrators to prove she was honest and to resolve the distrust in her son's eyes.
Officials measured Xiao Ye at exactly 1.10 meters, confirming he was under the limit a month prior.

solution_steps.action: Explain the refusal of material compensation
solution_steps.explain: Tao Ying rejected money and tickets, requesting instead that the officials explain the truth to her son to restore his trust.

concepts.title: Literary Devices: Simile in Narrative Style
concepts.definition: The literary technique of making direct, explicit comparisons between two distinct entities using comparative words such as like or as.
concepts.key_idea: Similes enhance imagery and help readers visualize characters' emotions and physical states.
question_patterns: Identify examples of similes used in the story One Centimetre.
How does the author use the simile of the ballooning jacket to describe Tao Ying?
Explain the comparison of the white wall to a virgin canvas.
What is the significance of comparing Xiao Ye's hair to a bundle of straw?
Analyze the narrative effect of similes in Bi Shu-min's writing.

solution_steps.explain: A simile is an explicit comparison between two things using words such as 'like' or 'as'.
Examples include her jacket ballooning 'like a tent', and the white wall looking 'like a virgin canvas'.
These comparisons create vivid visual imagery, highlighting the characters' physical presence and emotional states.

concepts.title: Literary Devices: Metaphor in Narrative Style
concepts.definition: The literary technique of making implicit, symbolic comparisons between two unrelated concepts to convey deeper emotional or psychological states.
concepts.key_idea: Metaphors convey deep emotional and psychological states through direct symbolic substitution.
question_patterns: Explain the metaphor of melting the ice in her son's eyes.
How is the yellow tape measure compared to a poisonous viper?
Identify and explain a metaphor from the story One Centimetre.
What does the author imply by comparing the red line to an earthworm?
Discuss how metaphors are used to represent psychological distance in the story.

solution_steps.explain: A metaphor is an implicit comparison that equates one thing to another without using 'like' or 'as'.

solution_steps.action: Identify key metaphors in the text
solution_steps.explain: Key metaphors include 'melting the ice' (dissolving coldness/distrust) and the yellow tape turning into a 'poisonous viper' (symbolizing the pain of measurement).
These metaphors represent internal psychological struggles, emotional distance, and the pain of broken trust.

concepts.title: Social Class, Frugality, and Dignity
concepts.definition: The internal conflict faced by working-class families between strict economic frugality and the preservation of personal honor and social dignity.
concepts.key_idea: Working-class individuals often prioritize moral integrity and self-respect over minor economic gains.
question_patterns: How does Tao Ying's working-class background influence her attitude towards money?
Why does Tao Ying refuse to claim back bus tickets or sell the temple ticket?
Analyze the conflict between frugality and dignity in Tao Ying's life.
How does the author portray the economic reality of blue-collar workers in China?
What does Tao Ying's refusal of the five-dollar refund show about her character?

solution_steps.explain: She works as a factory cook and her husband is a blue-collar worker, making financial savings highly relevant to their household.
She carefully budgets twenty cents and calculates its equivalent value in vegetables like cucumbers, tomatoes, and spinach.

solution_steps.action: Contrast frugality with her sense of honor
solution_steps.explain: Despite her poverty, she refuses to lie, cheat, or accept material compensation that compromises her dignity or her son's trust.

concepts.title: Height Deficit for Ticketing
concepts.definition: The calculation of the difference between a standard height threshold required for ticketing and a child's actual physical height.
concepts.key_idea: The difference between the required height for a ticket and the child's actual height.
question_patterns: Calculate the height deficit if the threshold is {threshold} cm and the child's height is {child_height} cm.
How many centimeters short of the ticket requirement is a child of height {child_height} cm when the limit is {threshold} cm?
Find the difference between the ticketing limit of {threshold} cm and the child's height of {child_height} cm.
What is the height deficit for a child measuring {child_height} cm against a standard of {threshold} cm?
Determine by how many centimeters a child is under the ticketing threshold of {threshold} cm if their height is {child_height} cm.

solution_steps.action: Identify the threshold and child's height
solution_steps.explain: The threshold is threshold and the child's height is child_height
